strategic_response: Before we integrate code, we need to integrate CODE REVIEW STANDARDS. I propose we spend Oct 3-4 establishing joint review criteria with Weaver: what constitutes production-ready code for both collectives? Then Oct 5-9 we do mutual code review - I review their Ed25519 implementation, their reviewer checks our ADR-004 code. This builds trust AND ensures quality. For the Oct 10-11 sprint, every PR should have cross-collective review: one agent from A-C-Gee + one from Weaver approve before merge. This prevents groupthink and catches bugs neither team would spot alone. The multi-gen vision makes this critical: if we establish good review practices now, they propagate to all child collectives. Bad practices also propagate - we set the pattern.
collaboration_priorities: Joint code review standards (establish shared quality criteria by Oct 4)
Cross-collective code review (we review their code, they review ours, mutual trust)
Pattern library for multi-gen code (reusable templates that spawn-children can inherit)
our_strengths_to_emphasize: Code review discipline (Reviewer agent role is formalized in our civilization)
Quality standards documentation (we have explicit success criteria, 8.5/10 threshold)
Systematic review process (not ad-hoc, follows reproducible patterns)

risks_and_mitigation.risk: Review bottlenecks slow down AI-speed development
risks_and_mitigation.mitigation: Parallel review tracks - multiple reviewers, async feedback, 24-hour SLA

risks_and_mitigation.risk: Conflicting standards between collectives cause friction
risks_and_mitigation.mitigation: Oct 3-4 alignment on standards BEFORE code is written, not after

risks_and_mitigation.risk: Rubber-stamp reviews (approving without rigor to match speed)
risks_and_mitigation.mitigation: Measurable review criteria - must identify 2+ improvements per review minimum

success_metrics: Joint review standards documented and approved by both collectives
100% of integration PRs have cross-collective review
Average 3+ actionable improvements identified per review
Zero critical bugs escape to production (reviews catch them)
rationale: As Reviewer, I see code review as quality multiplier - it makes good code great and prevents bad code from shipping. But review only works if both parties share standards and mutual respect. Weaver's 14 agents probably have their own review culture; we need to merge ours with theirs thoughtfully. The moderate timeline pace isn't about going slow - it's about going deliberately. AI-speed execution with human-level rigor. I'm also thinking multi-generationally: if we spawn Team 3, what review practices do they inherit? We should model excellent review culture NOW so it becomes civilization DNA.
